score.cap: grade limited to F: IPv4 INPUT accepts every new connection

findings.title: INPUT accepts new connections to any port
findings.detail: Rule #2 in filter/INPUT (-j ACCEPT) accepts them from any source, whatever the policy of the chain is. Every port that no rule names is open: a service that listens on one, now or later, is reachable at once.

fix.summary: This rule accepts every packet that reaches it, so the rules after it and the policy of the chain decide nothing. Add rules for the traffic that is needed, with a tested way back, then delete it.

steps.text: Delete the rule that accepts everything

findings.title: Unreachable rules in filter/INPUT
findings.detail: Rules #3-#5 (3 rules) are never reached: rule #2 (-j ACCEPT) ends the chain for all traffic before. 2 of them are DROP or REJECT and have no effect.

fix.summary: Delete the rules that are never reached, or move those that must apply above the rule that ends the chain.

If the clients are known, accept only their addresses. If SSH must stay open to any source, limit new connections for each source: the limit counts every source by itself, so one client cannot lock out the others, and it does not touch established sessions.

steps.text: Replace the rule with one for the known clients
Or drop the connections of a source that opens more than 10 a minute, in front of the rule
steps.command: iptables -I INPUT 1 -p tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4 -j DROP

findings.title: FORWARD accepts traffic that no rule names
findings.detail: No rule refuses it, and the policy of filter/FORWARD is ACCEPT. This matters when IP forwarding is enabled (net.ipv4.ip_forward, net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding): the host then routes packets between its networks without a filter.

fix.summary: Set the policy to DROP after the forwarding paths that are needed have rules.

findings.title: OUTPUT default policy is ACCEPT
findings.detail: All outbound traffic is allowed. This is the usual setup; an OUTPUT allowlist can limit what a compromised service is able to reach.

notes.text: No IPv6 rules were supplied: only IPv4 was analyzed, and IPv4 rules do not filter IPv6. Add the output of ip6tables-save as another file.
No list of listening sockets was read, so every open port is judged as if a service uses it. Add the output of "ss -tulnp" as another file to tell used ports from unused ones.

baseline.ipv4:
# Recommended IPv4 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (iptables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "iptables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s 127.0.0.0/8 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p icmp -m icmp --icmp-type 8 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh4-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
baseline.ipv6:
# Recommended IPv6 baseline generated by iptables-analyzer (ip6tables-restore format).
# Default deny inbound and forwarded traffic; outbound traffic is allowed.
# Apply with "ip6tables-restore --noflush": it replaces INPUT and keeps every
# other chain, including Docker's, intact.
*filter
:INPUT DROP [0:0]
:FORWARD DROP [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-F INPUT
-A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
# Neighbor discovery is untracked by conntrack and must be allowed explicitly;
# a hop limit of 255 proves the sender is on-link.
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 134 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "router advertisement (SLAAC)" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 135 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor solicitation" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 136 -m hl --hl-eq 255 -m comment --comment "neighbor advertisement" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 130 -m comment --comment "multicast listener query" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -s fe80::/10 -d fe80::/10 -p udp -m udp --sport 547 --dport 546 -m comment --comment "DHCPv6 client" -j ACCEPT
-A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate INVALID -j DROP
-A INPUT -s ::1/128 ! -i lo -j DROP
-A INPUT -p ipv6-icmp -m icmp6 --icmpv6-type 128 -m limit --limit 10/sec --limit-burst 20 -j ACCEPT
# Remote administration: new SSH connections are limited per source address.
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-above 10/min --hashlimit-burst 20 --hashlimit-mode srcip --hashlimit-name ssh6-22 -j DROP
-A INPUT -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j ACCEPT
COMMIT
notes: SSH is assumed on TCP port 22; change the port before applying if sshd listens elsewhere.
